headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channels, writes, or data flows are documented between RisingWave and Spring Integration samples.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented for risingwave and spring-integration-samples. Both profiles show network_egress:none and empty io_surfaces, so there is no plausible default injection route between them.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste channels.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
If a bridge is added, require provenance tagging on all exchanged text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and both report network_egress:none with no shared workspace or OAuth scopes. With no documented data flow from risingwave to spring-integration-samples, leakage is not plausible in the default pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of both runtimes.
Avoid shared OS accounts or mounted volumes.
Review any future connector or export path before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles expose no write surfaces, no concurrency model, and no permissions requested, so there is no documented overlapping mutable resource for risingwave and spring-integration-samples to contend over.
conditions: IF either agent is configured with write access to the same directory, database, or git repo, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories if writes are introduced.
Add locking before enabling any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pathway where spring-integration-samples consumes risingwave outputs as authoritative input, and neither profile shows downstream action authority. Without an input bridge, cascading error is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF one agent's output is wired into the other's decision-making or action pipeline, verify-before-act controls are needed.
mitigations: Insert a human or automated verification step before reuse of outputs.
Do not auto-execute actions from generated text.
Log provenance for any future handoff between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched, no residency-sensitive processing is documented, and both profiles are open-source docs-only entries. The pair does not show a compliance mismatch pathway on the available evidence, so the other agent is not separately implicated.
conditions: IF either profile begins processing regulated data or changes residency/retention policy, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Document any regulated-data handling before deployment.
Keep retention settings aligned if data classes are added.
Review jurisdictional requirements before connecting external services.
